why: Two reports become available in the same block, on different cores, guaranteed 5 slots apart. The accumulated-set entry is a SET — serialized in lexicographic hash order, not core order. This block is the only place in the family that exposes the difference.
family_explainer: The storage family runs a real service that stress-tests service storage. Each block: (1) new work reports are guaranteed onto cores, (2) validators assure availability of earlier reports, (3) once a report has a super-majority of assurances it becomes available and the service's ACCUMULATE entry point executes in the PVM — reading, writing and deleting storage keys via host calls, metered by gas. The post-state root certifies every byte: storage entries, the service's octet/item footprint, gas statistics, the accumulated-set ring and the ready queue.
events: Core 0: package 427d4736… guaranteed (5 work item(s), bundle 5227 bytes). It now waits on this core for availability assurances.
Core 1: package 75b26b80… guaranteed (1 work item(s), bundle 1095 bytes) — declares prerequisite ac9463be…. It now waits on this core for availability assurances.
6 validator assurance(s): core 0 has 6, core 1 has 6 vote(s). A report becomes AVAILABLE when votes exceed 2/3 of 6 validators (i.e. ≥ 5).

ACCUMULATION: package(s) a6a46aeb…, bf222778… became available and were accumulated — the service's accumulate entry point ran inside the PVM. The accumulated-set ring C(15) records them (sorted, ring 11), aging out after 12 blocks.
Service 0 statistics: 8 work item(s) accumulated for 309,354 gas (exact PVM metering — every instruction costs 1, host calls cost 10, log costs 10).
